For every admissible curve/residue data set in the stated manuscript, every finite row index N>=2 admits compatible coupled vector-field jets; choices admit a coefficientwise stable formal limit, without an analytic convergence assertion.

The jointly admissible inputs and finite jet at N=7 give a genuinely singular normal complex surface germ with full analytic derivation sheaf free of rank two and a resolution whose sole exceptional curve has genus 21 and self-intersection -10.

Every isolated normal complex analytic germ of dimension d>=1 with free analytic tangent module of rank d admits a normal integral finite-type affine C-model with the same marked completion, globally free algebraic derivations of rank d and smooth complement of the marked point.
There exists a finitely generated normal integral C-algebra A of dimension two with Der_C(A) isomorphic to A^2 and a nonregular localization at a maximal ideal.

external_assumptions.source: Source doi:10.1007/BF02684746; Section 1.6 Satz 4 and proof, p.15; section 2.1 Definition 3 and properties (a)-(c), p.16; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/analytic-realization/verdict.json. The usual analytic Noetherianity is also used; p.15 invokes Cartan-Ruckert, and the old report supplies a Weierstrass outline rather than claiming a new foundational proof.
external_assumptions.locator: Section 1.6 Satz 4 and proof, p.15; section 2.1 Definition 3 and properties (a)-(c), p.16

external_assumptions.statement: A compact nowhere-discrete analytic subset of a smooth complex surface is exceptional if and only if the intersection matrix of its irreducible components is negative definite. Exceptionality supplies a proper holomorphic contraction to a discrete set, a biholomorphism of complements and descent of holomorphic functions; the holomorphic reduction has connected fibers and normal target when its source is normal.
external_assumptions.source: Source doi:10.1007/BF01441136; Section 4.8(e), pp.366-367; section 2.4 Definition 3, pp.339-340; section 2.1, p.337; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/analytic-realization/verdict.json. Read the archived reader transcription of the primary pages and the source guide. The already constructed Hausdorff smooth surface and compact connected curve with matrix [-10] satisfy the hypotheses. Normality, properness, descent and connectedness are supplied by the cited definition/reduction passages, not merely inferred from the numerical matrix.
external_assumptions.locator: Section 4.8(e), pp.366-367; section 2.4 Definition 3, pp.339-340; section 2.1, p.337

external_assumptions.statement: For a proper holomorphic map pi:Y->X, a coherent source sheaf E, x in X and J=m_x O_Y, the m_x-adic completed stalk of R^q pi_*E is naturally isomorphic to the inverse limit of (R^q pi_*(E/J^rE))_x for ordinary powers r>=1. Quotient cohomology equals the needed direct-image stalk because the sheaves are supported on the compact infinitesimal fiber.
external_assumptions.locator: Section 6.5, definitions of the ideals preceding Hauptsatz II, and Hauptsatz IIa, p.59

external_assumptions.locator: Artin 1969, Theorem 1.10, printed page 26, PDF page 5; primary extraction lines 160-175

external_assumptions.statement: A Noetherian local ring and its maximal-ideal completion have equal Krull dimensions.

external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.97.1, parts (1)-(3)

external_assumptions.statement: If I lies in the Jacobson radical of a Noetherian ring R, R to its I-adic completion is faithfully flat. In particular this holds for maximal-ideal completion of every Noetherian local ring.

external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.97.3

external_assumptions.statement: A Noetherian local ring is regular if and only if its maximal-ideal completion is regular.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NY; Lemma 15.44.4; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.44.4

external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00U4; Lemma 10.143.5; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. The chosen pointed stage has equal residue field C, so together with nilpotent unique lifting its local completion is the chosen P.

external_assumptions.statement: Every etale ring map R to S admits a presentation S=R[z_1,...,z_n]/(h_1,...,h_n) in which det(partial h_j/partial z_i) is invertible in S.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00U9; Lemma 10.143.2; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. external_assumptions.statement: Fields and finite-type ring extensions of fields are excellent.

external_assumptions.locator: Proposition 15.53.3, parts (1) and (5)

external_assumptions.statement: The henselization of a local ring (R,m,kappa) is the filtered colimit of pointed etale R-algebras (S,q) with q over m and kappa(q)=kappa; its maximal ideal is mR^h and its residue field is kappa. Two represented elements are equal precisely when their images agree at a common later pointed stage.

external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.155.1 and the explicit construction and equality criterion in its proof

external_assumptions.statement: For a local ring R, Noetherianity is equivalent for R and R^h (also R^sh). In the Noetherian case Rhat to (R^h)hat is an isomorphism of complete local rings.

external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.46.3, Noetherian equivalences and part (b)

external_assumptions.statement: If (R,m) is a normal Noetherian local ring whose formal fibres are normal, then Rhat is normal; excellence or quasi-excellence is a sufficient formal-fibre hypothesis.

external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.53.6

external_assumptions.locator: Grauert 1960, section 1.6 Satz 4 and proof, page 15; section 2.1 Definition 3 and properties (a)-(c), page 16

external_assumptions.statement: If I lies in the Jacobson radical of a Noetherian ring R, R to its I-adic completion is faithfully flat. In particular this holds for maximal-ideal completion of every Noetherian local ring.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00MC; Lemma 10.97.3; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to S and T; justifies finite-kernel base change, vanishing detection and ideal contraction.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.97.3

external_assumptions.statement: A Noetherian local ring is regular if and only if its maximal-ideal completion is regular.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NY; Lemma 15.44.4; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. Completion preserves both dimension and embedding dimension, so a singular marked analytic point remains nonregular algebraically.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.44.4

external_assumptions.statement: For X=Spec(S), S a finite-type algebra over a field, topological dim_x(X) equals the maximum dimension of the irreducible components passing through x.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OT; Lemma 10.114.5, equivalence of (1) and (2); read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. Topological dimension is d everywhere on the retained integral neighborhood; local-ring dimension at a nonclosed point is not substituted.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.114.5, equivalence of (1) and (2)

external_assumptions.statement: For a finite-type integral-domain algebra S over a field, dim(S)=dim(S_m) for every maximal ideal m.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OS; Lemma 10.114.4; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. The marked point is closed with residue C; the retained domain therefore has global dimension dim(T)=d.

external_assumptions.statement: If R to S is etale at a prime q over p, then pS_q=qS_q is the maximal ideal of S_q, and kappa(q)/kappa(p) is finite separable.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00U4; Lemma 10.143.5; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. The chosen pointed stage has equal residue field C, so together with nilpotent unique lifting its local completion is the chosen P.

external_assumptions.statement: Every etale ring map R to S admits a presentation S=R[z_1,...,z_n]/(h_1,...,h_n) in which det(partial h_j/partial z_i) is invertible in S.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00U9; Lemma 10.143.2; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. Invertible auxiliary Jacobian gives the differential basis and the nilpotent lifting argument for the pointed completion.

external_assumptions.statement: Etale maps are stable under localization, composition and base change. Etale algebras descend over filtered colimits; in particular an etale algebra over a localization S^(-1)A is the localization of an etale A-algebra.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00U2; Lemma 10.143.3, parts (1)-(3), (9), (10); read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived parts and current primary tag read. Finite presentation and finitely many point-preserving denominators spread the stage and its entries/identities to one finite-type affine etale C[x]-algebra.

external_assumptions.statement: Fields and finite-type ring extensions of fields are excellent.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07QW; Proposition 15.53.3, parts (1) and (5); read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to the retained finite-type C-domain after removing nilpotents and unwanted components.
external_assumptions.locator: Proposition 15.53.3, parts (1) and (5)

external_assumptions.statement: The henselization of a local ring (R,m,kappa) is the filtered colimit of pointed etale R-algebras (S,q) with q over m and kappa(q)=kappa; its maximal ideal is mR^h and its residue field is kappa. Two represented elements are equal precisely when their images agree at a common later pointed stage.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04GN; Lemma 10.155.1 and the explicit construction and equality criterion in its proof; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement, current primary statement in raw HTML, and filtered-category proof read. Finite entries and all finite zero-product identities descend together; injectivity of a stage is not assumed.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 10.155.1 and the explicit construction and equality criterion in its proof

external_assumptions.statement: For a local ring R, Noetherianity is equivalent for R and R^h (also R^sh). In the Noetherian case Rhat to (R^h)hat is an isomorphism of complete local rings.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06LJ; Lemma 15.46.3, Noetherian equivalences and part (b); read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. Applies to Q0=C[x]_(x) and H=Q0^h; H itself is not identified with P.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.46.3, Noetherian equivalences and part (b)

external_assumptions.statement: A quasi-excellent ring is Nagata. In particular a quasi-excellent domain is N-1 and has finite normalization in its fraction field.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07QV; Lemma 15.53.5 and its proof's N-1 conclusion; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag/proof read. The finite normalization quotient vanishes after localization at the already normal T; killing that quotient yields a normal open without changing T.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.53.5 and its proof's N-1 conclusion

external_assumptions.statement: If (R,m) is a normal Noetherian local ring whose formal fibres are normal, then Rhat is normal; excellence or quasi-excellence is a sufficient formal-fibre hypothesis.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C23; Lemma 15.53.6; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. The analytic normality is a hypothesis; Cutkosky v3 supplies excellence. Normality alone is not used to infer normal completion.
external_assumptions.locator: Lemma 15.53.6

external_assumptions.statement: For a finite-type k-algebra S, k a field, and a prime q corresponding to x in X=Spec(S), smoothness at q is equivalent to dim_kappa(q)(Omega_(S/k) tensor kappa(q))<=dim_x(X), equivalently equality. In that case S_q is regular.
external_assumptions.source: Source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TT; Lemma 10.140.3; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Archived statement and current primary tag read. On the integral d-dimensional neighborhood, the minimal-generator minor criterion identifies V(Fitt_d(Omega)) with the nonsmooth locus.

external_assumptions.statement: Analytic structure sheaves are coherent; kernels, cokernels, images, tensor products and Hom of coherent analytic sheaves are coherent. The nilradical has a uniform nilpotence exponent on relatively compact subsets, including for nonreduced complex spaces.
external_assumptions.source: Source doi:10.1007/BF02684746; Grauert 1960, section 1.6 Satz 4 and proof, page 15; section 2.1 Definition 3 and properties (a)-(c), page 16; read passage recorded in research/draft_reviews/affine-algebraization/verdict.json. Primary extracted pages read; this is also a version-matched historical analytic input. Coherence provides finite conormal-dual kernels and cokernels. Uniform nilpotence is not silently substituted for the separate isolated-zero-set argument.
external_assumptions.locator: Grauert 1960, section 1.6 Satz 4 and proof, page 15; section 2.1 Definition 3 and properties (a)-(c), page 16
